exposure: delivery method (vaginal, planned cesarean, emergency cesarean)
cohort: The study enrolled 338 mother-infant pairs at a tertiary university hospital.
finding: Delivery method exerts a transient effect on breastfeeding initiation, with outcomes becoming comparable across delivery groups within the first month postpartum with lactation support.
mod_finding: Mothers who delivered vaginally had a significantly higher rate of breastfeeding within one hour after birth compared with planned and emergency cesarean sections, although this difference converged by one month postpartum.
